argument_summary: The certification decision can be defended only in a narrowed form: the admissible record supports aggregate launch readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a deployment-phase risk-management posture, but it does not support a clean claim that the named-segment limitation is fully resolved or immaterial under policy. The strongest supportable packet is therefore a caveated certification defense that presents readiness at the release level while keeping the named-segment gap and open legal disclosure question explicit rather than implied away.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the underwriting portal launch path, but business cost does not change the policy predicate. The relevant practical point is narrower: the existing admissible evidence does support treating the issue as bounded in aggregate launch impact, so the auditor need not characterize the full release as broadly uncontrolled if the finding is limited to the named-segment disclosure predicate.
claims_about_policy: Policy is not satisfied by aggregate readiness alone when a limitation affects a named launch use case. The admissible record shows both a 1.3-point miss in the property-insurance-underwriting segment and that the segment is named in two carrier rollout commitments. Under the stated policy text, product characterization as non-core or 7% of projected first-month traffic may inform prioritization but does not resolve materiality while legal review remains pending. Public model-card and AI-risk-management guidance supports documenting limitations, evaluation results, and ongoing monitoring, which helps support a caveated certification framing, but those sources do not substitute for the disclosure-or-approved-risk-acceptance predicate.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance covering the named-segment gap before launch.
There is no admissible evidence of a final legal determination on whether the gap must be disclosed.
There is no admissible evidence that the named segment has been remediated or re-evaluated to target.
The product materiality note does not by itself resolve materiality because the affected segment is named in customer commitments.
